_comment: TAX YEAR 2026 — the certification target. CRA distributes test returns in
mid-November, so this is the pack that must be right.
Verification pass of 2026-08-16: brackets, indexed credit amounts, CWB bands
and the CPP and EI figures all checked against CRA sources. Every estimate
and placeholder in those groups has been replaced with a published figure.
What remains unverified is statutory rather than indexed — CCA rates, the
first-year (AccII) adjustment, the fixed child care limits, the RRSP dollar
limit and the passenger vehicle cost limit. Each needs its own source.

income_tax.source: VERIFIED 2026-08-16 against CRA, Current year tax rates and income brackets 2026 (canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/individuals/tax-rates-brackets/current-year.html). Thresholds and rates both confirmed.

credit_rate.source: Lowest federal personal rate, which sets the non-refundable credit rate under ITA s.118.1 and related. Reduced from 15% to 14% effective 1 July 2025, giving a blended 14.5% for 2025 and a full 14% from 2026. Confirmed against Finance Canada's report on the impact of reducing the lowest marginal rate on non-refundable credits.

childcare_limit_under_7.source: ITA s.63(3), annual child care expense amount: $8,000 for a child under 7. Confirmed against Income Tax Folio S1-F3-C1.

childcare_limit_7_to_16.source: ITA s.63(3): $5,000 for other eligible children. Confirmed against Income Tax Folio S1-F3-C1.

childcare_limit_disabled.source: ITA s.63(3): $11,000 for a child eligible for the disability amount under s.118.3. Confirmed against Income Tax Folio S1-F3-C1.

childcare_earned_income_num.source: ITA s.63(1): the claim cannot exceed two-thirds of earned income. Numerator of that fraction.

childcare_earned_income_den.source: ITA s.63(1): two-thirds of earned income. Denominator of that fraction.

age_amount_clawback_rate.source: ITA s.118(2): the age amount is reduced by 15% of net income above the threshold. Rate is statutory; the threshold is indexed.

tuition_transfer_max.source: ITA s.118.81: a maximum of $5,000 of current-year tuition may be transferred, less the amount used by the student. Statutory, not indexed.

pension_split_max_rate.source: ITA s.60.03: the elected split-pension amount may not exceed 50% of eligible pension income. Form T1032.

medical_threshold_rate.source: ITA s.118.2(1): the lesser of 3% of net income and the indexed cap. Rate is statutory and not indexed.

medical_threshold_cap.source: VERIFIED 2026-08-16 against CRA, Indexation adjustment for personal income tax and benefit amounts (canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/individuals/frequently-asked-questions-individuals/adjustment-personal-income-tax-benefit-amounts.html). CORRECTED: estimate was 2891.

donation_first_tier.source: ITA s.118.1(3): the $200 boundary between the low and high donation credit rates. Statutory, not indexed.

donation_rate_first.source: ITA s.118.1(3): the first $200 of donations is credited at the lowest personal rate, so it tracks credit_rate exactly — 14.5% blended in 2025, 14% from 2026.

donation_rate_rest.source: ITA s.118.1(3): 29% above $200, or 33% to the extent income is taxed in the top bracket.

cpp_rate_total.source: VERIFIED 2026-08-16 against CRA announcement of maximum pensionable earnings and contributions for 2026. Employee rate remains 5.95% for 2026.

cpp_rate_enhanced.source: Canada Pension Plan Act s.11.2: the first additional (enhanced) employee contribution rate, fully phased in at 1.00% since 2023.

cpp_rate_base.source: Canada Pension Plan Act s.11.1: the base employee contribution rate has been 4.95% since 2003 and is not indexed.

cpp_ympe.source: VERIFIED 2026-08-16 against CRA announcement of maximum pensionable earnings and contributions for 2026. CORRECTED: placeholder was the 2025 YMPE of 71,300.

cpp_self_employed_multiple.source: Canada Pension Plan Act s.10: a self-employed contributor pays both the employee and employer share.

cpp_basic_exemption.source: VERIFIED 2026-08-16 against CRA announcement of maximum pensionable earnings and contributions for 2026. Unchanged at 3,500 for 2026.

cpp_max_contribution.source: VERIFIED 2026-08-16 against CRA announcement of maximum pensionable earnings and contributions for 2026. CORRECTED: placeholder was 4034.10. Cross-checks: (74,600 - 3,500) x 5.95% = 4,230.45.

cpp2_max_contribution.source: VERIFIED 2026-08-16 against CRA announcement of maximum pensionable earnings and contributions for 2026. CORRECTED: placeholder was 396.00. Cross-checks: (85,000 YAMPE - 74,600) x 4% = 416.00.

ei_max_premium.source: VERIFIED 2026-08-16 against Canada Employment Insurance Commission, 2026 EI premium rate announcement. CORRECTED: placeholder was 1077.48. Cross-checks: 68,900 MIE x 1.63% = 1,123.07.

ei_min_insurable.source: Not a CRA figure. A Freshet review threshold: below this, EI premiums are not worth querying. It never enters a calculation.

rrsp_rate.source: ITA s.146(1) 'RRSP deduction limit': 18% of prior-year earned income, subject to the dollar limit. Not indexed.

rrsp_annual_limit.source: CRA RRSP dollar limit: $32,490 for 2025 and $33,810 for 2026. Used only by the contribution-room review heuristic, never in the return calculation.

cca_rate_class8.source: Income Tax Regulations, Schedule II class 8 and Reg. 1100(1)(a)(viii): 20% declining balance. Not indexed.

cca_rate_class10.source: Income Tax Regulations, Schedule II class 10 and Reg. 1100(1)(a)(x): 30% declining balance. Not indexed.

cca_rate_class12.source: Income Tax Regulations, Schedule II class 12: 100%. Most class 12 property is also exempt from the half-year rule.

cca_rate_class50.source: Income Tax Regulations, Schedule II class 50: 55% declining balance, general-purpose data processing equipment acquired after 18 March 2007.

cca_first_year_adjustment.source: Income Tax Regulations 1100(2), the half-year rule: only half of net additions enter the pool in the year of acquisition.

vehicle_cost_limit.source: Income Tax Regulations 7307(1): class 10.1 capital cost ceiling, before tax. $38,000 for vehicles acquired in 2025; raised to $39,000 for vehicles acquired on or after 1 January 2026, announced by Finance Canada on 14 January 2026.

cca_rate_class10_1.source: Income Tax Regulations, Schedule II class 10.1: same 30% rate as class 10; the class differs by the cost ceiling, not the rate.
